Automated Decision-Making 7
The University is committed to ensuring transparency, fairness and accountability in all
automated decision-making processes including by:
assessment of the impact of the automated decision-making processes;
regular review to minimise bias and ensure compliance with applicable privacy laws; and
taking reasonable steps to notify individuals of use of automated decision-making processes.
The University, during its functions and activities, may:
use computer programs, including rule-based systems and artificial intelligence or machine
learning technologies; and
use or engage in third-party services that use computer programs, including rule-based
systems and artificial intelligence or machine learning technologies,
to assist or support in the review and decision-making which could significantly affect
individual rights or interests.
Where these decisions relate to eligibility for services, access to benefits, or other outcomes
that may significantly affect an individual, the University will take reasonable steps to notify
individuals of the:
types of Personal Information used;
nature of decisions made; and
human intervention and review controls in place.
Individuals may request human review of decisions that significantly affect them where
automated decision-making has been used.

Privacy Officer
For the purposes of Part 2 of the PRIS Act, the University designates the Director, Strategic and
Governance Services as its Privacy Officer.
The Privacy Officer is the senior officer responsible for strategic oversight of the University’s
compliance with this policy and applicable privacy legislation together with the development,
maintenance and oversight of the University’s privacy management approach, including:
the University’s privacy management practices;
privacy complaints or concerns in line with the Complaints Policy;
identification, assessment and articulation of privacy risks in line with the ECU Risk
Management Framework to enable ECU to make informed risk-based decisions;
Privacy Impact Assessments with University stakeholders and wider University community as
necessary; and
investigation and response to Information Breach Incident reports (in line with Critical Incident
and Business Continuity Management Policy and supporting procedures and other operational
documents).

documents_checked.text:
The PIA will ensure privacy considerations are embedded early in the planning and operational
activities for all initiatives - projects, programs, systems, or changes in processes that:
Collect, use, store, disclose, or transfer personal information;
Introduce new or significantly changed ways of handling personal information;
Are likely to have a high rated privacy risk or significant impact on individuals’ privacy.
Step 1 – Privacy Threshold Assessment
For every initiative involving new or changed ways of handling personal information, the
Project Officer or Manager must conduct a Privacy Threshold Assessment (PTA).
The PTA is in the format of a short questionnaire to triage if further detailed Privacy Impact
Assessment is required.
Depending on the outcome of the PTA, some assessments will end at this point. Some will
proceed to Step 2 Conduct a PIA.
Step 2 – Conduct a Privacy Impact Assessment
The PIA is comprised of a number of questions to guide Staff through a systematic assessment
of the initiative.
The Project Officer or Manager are responsible for initiating and completing the PIA.
The PIA must be approved by the Project Sponsor.
The PIA must be submitted to Privacy team (Privacy@ECU).
The Privacy Officer or delegate will assess the PIA.

Collection Notices
The University will provide relevant collection notices that set out the purpose for collecting
Personal Information and Sensitive Personal Information in accordance with this policy.
At or before the collection of Personal Information, or as soon as practicable thereafter, the
University will take reasonable steps to notify the individual or ensure that the individual is
aware of the collection, and that the collection is fair and reasonable in the circumstances.
The notification must contain the following and may take the form of a collection notice or
other appropriate forms of communication (including digital interfaces, system notices, or
contractual arrangements):
the University’s contact details;
where the University has collected this information from someone other than directly from the
individual or where the individual may not be aware the University has collected the
information, the fact that the information has been collected and circumstances around its
collection;
how the individual may request access or correction to information, including through the FOI
Act processes;
the purpose for collecting the information, and any laws that require the particular information
to be collected (if applicable);

documents_checked.text:
The University will take steps to reasonably ensure that the Personal Information it collects,
uses, or discloses is accurate, up-to-date and complete.
The University recognises that, under the PRIS Act, the Information Privacy Principle relating to
access and correction does not apply to agencies subject to the FOI Act, and that requests for
access to, and correction of, Personal Information for the University are primarily governed
under the FOI Act mechanisms.
The University may, at its discretion, provide access to Personal Information outside of the FOI
Act where it is reasonable and practicable to do so. The University may decline informal
requests where it considers it appropriate to require a formal application under the FOI Act.
Individuals may apply or request access to their own Personal Information or correction of this
Personal Information by contacting the relevant University area, or by application to the
Privacy Officer.
The University will aim to respond to informal access or correction requests within 45 days,
noting that statutory timeframes apply where requests are made under the FOI Act. If the
University determines that it is not reasonable to allow access or amend an individual’s
Personal Information, it will inform the individual of the reasons for denial of access or
correction.
Individuals may also apply under the FOI Act for an amendment of Personal Information.

This policy applies to:
Complaints made by prospective, current and former Students or members of the public about
the University or University-related conduct, whether occurring in Australia or overseas; and
all persons involved in making, responding to, managing or resolving those Complaints.
Where legislation or another University or external framework provides a specific process for
dealing with all or part of a matter, the University may refer or manage that matter under the
applicable process. This includes matters concerning academic review or appeal, public
interest disclosures, misconduct, staff performance, privacy, employment or workplace
grievances, the ECU Student Guild, and third-party organisations.
This does not prevent the University from considering a distinct Complaint about its
administration of, or response to, the matter.
Where a matter engages more than one framework, the University will determine whether the
relevant issues are to be managed separately, sequentially, concurrently or in a coordinated
manner and will inform the Complainant of the applicable pathway.

Collection Notices
The University will provide relevant collection notices that set out the purpose for collecting
Personal Information and Sensitive Personal Information in accordance with this policy.
At or before the collection of Personal Information, or as soon as practicable thereafter, the
University will take reasonable steps to notify the individual or ensure that the individual is
aware of the collection, and that the collection is fair and reasonable in the circumstances.
The notification must contain the following and may take the form of a collection notice or
other appropriate forms of communication (including digital interfaces, system notices, or
contractual arrangements):
the University’s contact details;
where the University has collected this information from someone other than directly from the
individual or where the individual may not be aware the University has collected the
information, the fact that the information has been collected and circumstances around its
collection;
how the individual may request access or correction to information, including through the FOI
Act processes;
the purpose for collecting the information, and any laws that require the particular information
to be collected (if applicable);

documents_checked.text:
The University will take steps to reasonably ensure that the Personal Information it collects,
uses, or discloses is accurate, up-to-date and complete.
The University recognises that, under the PRIS Act, the Information Privacy Principle relating to
access and correction does not apply to agencies subject to the FOI Act, and that requests for
access to, and correction of, Personal Information for the University are primarily governed
under the FOI Act mechanisms.
The University may, at its discretion, provide access to Personal Information outside of the FOI
Act where it is reasonable and practicable to do so. The University may decline informal
requests where it considers it appropriate to require a formal application under the FOI Act.
Individuals may apply or request access to their own Personal Information or correction of this
Personal Information by contacting the relevant University area, or by application to the
Privacy Officer.
The University will aim to respond to informal access or correction requests within 45 days,
noting that statutory timeframes apply where requests are made under the FOI Act. If the
University determines that it is not reasonable to allow access or amend an individual’s
Personal Information, it will inform the individual of the reasons for denial of access or
correction.
Individuals may also apply under the FOI Act for an amendment of Personal Information.
